# Machine-use demo walkthrough (demos/machine-use.md)

## Goal

Author the user-facing walkthrough that motivates and demonstrates the
JSON-driven reporting workflow, driving the reporting script delivered by
TF-0MUX0XKCC0088GV4.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `demos/machine-use.md` exists with valid front matter (`title`, `id: machine-use`, `description`) and `##` step headings, following `demos/README.md`.
2. The walkthrough motivates the problem (choosing new placeholder sounds without reusing already-placed ones), shows raw `toneforge list recipes --category card-game --json` output, runs `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` (human-readable then `--json`), and shows the JSON report composing with further tooling (e.g. a generation queue), noting human output is unchanged.
3. Every executable `bash` code block uses `toneforge` as the command name and is runnable/headless.
4. The file parses cleanly with `src/demo/parser.ts` and satisfies the existing `src/demo/parser.integration.test.ts` constraints (valid front matter, ≥1 step, ≥1 toneforge command).
5. The walkthrough references the committed fixture and the reporting script paths accurately.

## Key Files

- `demos/machine-use.md` — new walkthrough.
- `demos/README.md` — convention reference; index update is a separate docs item.
- `demos/recipe-filtering.md` (Act 7) — narrative precedent for `list recipes --json`.
- `demos/batch-generation.md` — precedent for a batch-oriented walkthrough.
- `scripts/report-available-sounds.sh` — the script the walkthrough drives.

## Dependencies

Blocked by TF-0MUX0XKCC0088GV4 (script + fixture + test).

# Semver and dependency conflict detection

## Goal

Enforce semantic versioning and detect version conflicts with actionable errors so a
dependency bump cannot silently break builds (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 5,
9, 11).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Semver parsing, comparison and range compatibility are implemented (or delegated to a
   vetted minimal implementation) without adding an unjustified runtime dependency.
2. Missing, circular and incompatible-major dependencies each produce a distinct,
   actionable structured error.
3. Resolution is deterministic and independent of input ordering.
4. Unit tests cover each conflict class and the compatible case and precede the
   implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`: semver helpers plus dependency resolution and conflict
  classification.
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`: tests written first, using F1 fixtures.
- Prefer a small in-repo implementation over a new dependency (`package.json` currently
  has no semver library).

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Semver + dependency resolution helpers.
- Structured conflict errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
data.title: Semver and dependency conflict detection

# Marketplace install pipeline

## Goal

Deliver `install(package@version)` end-to-end: fetch -> integrity check -> validate ->
register assets -> version lock + provenance (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7,
8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Install fetches from the registry, verifies content-hash integrity, validates the
   manifest and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages and integrity failures are rejected **before** any local
   registration occurs.
3. A successful install registers recipes/stacks/sequences/palettes, records provenance
   and locks the exact version.
4. Re-installing the same version is reproducible (identical registered state and
   byte-identical outputs).
5. Unit and integration tests use the fixture registry only (no live network).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`: orchestrate the pipeline against the F3 registry and F4
  resolver, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`: tests written first; failure paths before success.
- Registration into the library/recipe registry is completed by F8.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Install pipeline with integrity, validation, version lock and provenance.
- Unit + integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.
data.title: Marketplace install pipeline

# Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate

## Goal

Deliver `publish(packageDir, name, version)` that validates a package (including the
Demo 12 Validator), rejects invalid packages with structured errors, and publishes
immutably (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7, 9).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Publish validates manifest/schema, dependency resolution, determinism checks, license
   declaration and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages are rejected with structured errors and nothing is published.
3. Published versions are immutable; republishing an existing version fails with an
   actionable error.
4. Unit tests cover the reject and publish paths via the fixture registry.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`: validation orchestration + immutable write to the
  registry adapter, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`: tests written first; rejection paths before success.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Publish pipeline with Validator gate and immutability.
- Structured rejection errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.

# Marketplace CLI command group

## Goal

Expose the Marketplace through a `marketplace` command group registered in the yargs CLI,
with the documented `--json` contracts (`docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` Demo 16).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `toneforge marketplace search --category <c>` returns listings and supports `--json`.
2. `toneforge marketplace install <package>@<version>` installs and reports the
   registered assets, and supports `--json`.
3. `toneforge marketplace publish --package <dir> --name <n> --version <v>` validates
   and publishes, and supports `--json`.
4. The `marketplace` group is registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts` and appears in CLI help.
5. CLI integration tests cover all three commands and their `--json` contracts.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`: command module following the
  `src/cli/commands/library.ts` pattern.
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`: register the group.
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`: tests written first against the fixture
  registry.

## Key Files:

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Marketplace CLI group (search/install/publish) with `--json`.
- CLI integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).
- F6 (Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate).
data.title: Marketplace CLI command group

# Register installed assets into library and recipe registry

## Goal

Make installed marketplace assets usable immediately by registering them through the
existing library index store and recipe registry rather than a forked store
(`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Installed recipes are available immediately via
   `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>`.
2. Installed stacks render via `toneforge stack render`.
3. Registration reuses the existing `src/library/` index store and
   `src/core/recipe.ts` registry (extend, do not fork), plus Demo 7 conventions where
   present.
4. An installed asset produces byte-identical output to an equivalent locally authored
   asset for the same seed.
5. Integration tests cover `generate` and `stack render` against a fixture install.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/library/index-store.ts` and `src/core/recipe.ts` registration helpers as
  needed.
- Wire registration from `src/marketplace/install.ts` into the existing registry.
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`: tests written first.

## Key Files:

- `src/library/index-store.ts`
- `src/core/recipe.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Installed assets registered into the local registry.
- Determinism integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).

data.comment:
Implementation notes (F5 install pipeline)

Files: src/marketplace/install.ts, src/marketplace/install.test.ts, src/marketplace/index.ts (exports), src/marketplace/types.ts (optional bundle.integrity).

Pipeline: fetch -> integrity (path-safety + existence + SHA-256 + optional declared-hash compare) -> validation gate -> dependency resolution (F4, opt-in) -> register (content-addressed assets, provenance, exact version lock). All rejection paths return before any side effect; the registrar (F8 hook) and install-state store are reached only after every gate passes.

Design decisions / assumptions:
- Demo 12 Validator seam: MarketplaceValidator + createValidatorGate is the injectable quality gate. The default gate (createManifestValidator) re-validates the manifest schema and asserts JSON assets parse. Demo 12 audio validation requires rendered LibraryEntry objects, which a JSON package does not carry, so the concrete Demo 12 wiring belongs at the CLI/publish boundary (F6/F7) through the same seam. Proven by the injected-gate rejection test.
- Reproducibility: records are content-addressed with no timestamps; state is normalised (packages by name, assets by id) so re-install and independent stores produce byte-identical serialised state.
- Version lock: exactly one installed record per package name, pinned to the installed version.
- Dependency conflicts (F4) are opt-in via an injected DependencyProvider so the pipeline stays registry-agnostic; F7 supplies a provider built from the index + installed state.
- Added an optional MarketplacePackageBundle.integrity map (additive) so declared content hashes can be verified; the local adapter without one still verifies presence/readability and computes hashes.
